G - WRITINGS OF THE SERVANT OF GOD

Under this title we present the votes of the theologian censors on the writings of the Servant of God and other studies on them.

The quantity of material to be examined required of the censors some years of work, during which a difficulty arose on account of one of the writings: the volume Labors and Consolations, which already during the life of the Servant of God had provoked the Apostolic Visit (cf. Summ., pp. 6-7). We therefore consider it useful to summarize the iter of the question and its solution with the relevant documents.

The writings of the Servant of God were handed over to the Congregation of Rites in 1927; on 15 June of the same year Card. Aurelio Galli was elected Ponens and the following year the censors of the writings were elected. On 18 December 1929, in place of the deceased Card. Galli, Card. Alessandro Verde was elected Ponens.

By letter of 1 April 1932 n. R 16/32 the Congregation of Rites asked the Supreme Congregation of the Holy Office for the Nihil obstat for the introduction of the cause, but on 15 April the Holy Office replied: «On the part of this Supreme Holy Congregation nothing stands in the way of the introduction of the following causes of beatification: 1. Maria Francesca De Siedliska (…); 2. Pio Brunone Lanteri (…); 3. Luigi Guanella (…). As to the introduction of the Cause of Beatification of Rosa Gattorno, foundress of the Institute of the Daughters of St. Anne, the same Holy Congregation has replied: “Dilata”» (cf. infra n. 5a). The letter made no mention of the reasons for this decision.

The first censor of the writings, Fr. Apollinare Perez OSA, finished his work in 1931 (cf. infra n. 1); the second censor, Fr. Stefano Ignudi OFMC, finished it two years after the dilata, that is, in 1934, and expressed the opinion that in the writings of the Servant of God nothing prevented proceeding further (cf. infra n. 2).

From 1932 to 1948 there were various interventions by the Cardinal Dean of the Sacred College, Gennaro Granito Pignatelli di Belmonte, that the dilata be removed and the cause be able to proceed. Each request was followed by a long examination on the part of the Holy Office of the volume Labors and Consolations, which invariably ended with the confirmation of the dilata, as appears from the examination of the documentation existing at the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith.

Among the documents the letter addressed to the Holy Father by the Promoter General of the Faith, Mons. Salvatore Natucci, dated 27 January 1937 (cf. infra n. 5c.), is of notable importance; in it he states that «the cause (of the Servant of God) appears most noble», as he was able to ascertain from the diligent examination of the Informative Process and from the report received from Fr. Ignudi (cf. infra n. 5d.), censor of the writings, to whom he turned for greater prudence of judgment.

In 1960 the Postulator d. Giulio Bianchini addressed a letter to the Holy Father so that the Cause might continue (cf. infra n. 5e.), but the Holy Office, when consulted, replied that the dilata of 1932 remained in full force (cf. infra n. 5f.).

On 20 January 1978 the postulator Fr. Antonio Cairoli addressed a petition to the Prefect of the Congregation for the Causes of Saints asking him to ask the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith the reasons for the dilata (cf. infra n. 5g).

By letter dated 3 April 1979 the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith replied that it granted the Nihil obstat for the cause of beatification, but expressed the wish that in the examination of the Cause there be studied «the state of normality or not of the Servant of God, with express indication of its nature and its degree in relation to impairment of the personality» (cf. infra n. 5h.).

For this study requested by the former Holy Office the Congregation for the Causes of Saints appointed an expert in the person of Dr. Fr. Paolino Zavarella, who delivered his vote on 7 December 1982. In it he states that, having examined the book Labors and Consolations and compared it with the life, the work and the other writings of the Servant of God, he could affirm that Rosa Gattorno «was not only normal from the psychic point of view but was a person rich in high qualities» and that the examination made showed «a perfect self-mastery, a more than notable psychic balance, great capacities for achievement and (especially in the vast correspondence) a continual exercise of charity in understanding, directing, comforting others» (cf. infra n. 3).

1. Opinion of the Most Rev. Fr. Apollinare Pérez OSA, First Censor of the writings of the Servant of God, dated 16 December 1931.

To the Most Eminent and Most Reverend Lord Cardinal Verde, Ponens in the Cause of Beatification and Canonization of the Servant of God Sister Anna Rosa Gattorno, Foundress of the Religious Institute of the Sisters Daughters of St. Anne

Most Eminent Prince

Designated by Your Most Reverend Eminence Theologian Censor of the writings of the Servant of God Sister Anna Rosa Gattorno, I was summoned to the Chancery of the Sacred Congregation of Rites to take the prescribed oath before the Most Illustrious Chancellor-Notary of the same Congregation. This done, the same Chancellor handed over to me the following writings:

1° Envelopes or fascicles 14. They contain autograph manuscripts of the S.G. under the title - Memoirs - They begin with these words: In the year 1857, having remained free of every bond, I devoted myself with more fervor to pious works and to frequenting the hospitals, the poor sick at home, assisting them, helping them as much as I could and serving them in everything…

The Memoirs continue to the year 1895 without any division into chapters or articles; the only division is given in parts or small and separate fascicles; each of them has distinct pages. Thus: Fascicle No. 1 divided into two parts, of which the first numbers 196 pages and the other 122= Fascicle No. 2, p. 187= Fasc. No. 3, p. 83= Fasc. They contain letters =Letters of the Servant of God=; to enumerate them all one by one would be too prolix, it is enough to say that, in sum, according to the list, they are 8451 at the least. Of these, 2363 were written and signed by another hand, in the name, however, of the Servant of God.

Such are those contained in Fasc. No. 66-67-68-72-77 and two in fasc. 71. There are another 52 signed only by the S.G., which are found in Fasc. No. 70, 46 letters, and in Fasc. No. 71, 6 letters. These are the writings I received; I read them all diligently and attentively in order to fulfill rightly the charge entrusted to me; but before giving my judgment on the doctrine, I shall briefly indicate the argument of the writings and the purpose of the author.

The autograph writings under the title =Memoirs= are the autobiography of the S.G., in which she narrates almost day by day the principal things that happened to her, above all her great tribulations, infirmities and assiduous labors, to use her own words, in the work of the Lord, that is, in the foundation and government of the Institute of the Daughters of St. Anne; very often she recounts the diabolical suggestions she suffered, the horrendous visions and images of various beasts with which the demons tried to terrify her; and how she, by prayer and a prompt and trusting refuge in her dear Crucifix, repelled all the snares of the infernal enemy. With a grateful heart she also manifests the heavenly favors and consoling visions with which her soul was refreshed.

Fascicle No. 2 contains the history of the foundation of the Institute of the Daughters of St. Anne from the beginning to the Decree of Praise. In the same fascicle there are 47 brief meditations which the S.G. made in Lent of the year 1864 on the Passion of J.C.

The motive or purpose of writing these Memoirs is sufficiently clear from the words of the S.G.: she wrote them from a certain inner impulse which she felt, or by a secret voice ordering her to write and suggesting the things to say, and at times her silence was rebuked. The second part of fascicle No. 1 begins with these words: «Year 1864. Ah! beautiful and great things He let me see in these contemplations of 1864. I would like to write so many things, but I shall always say that if my Jesus wished, He would surely make me move the pen as it pleases Him, so He would give me an angelic prompter so that I might describe them as I see them, feel them. But, firm in this principle, I set to the work, sure that I shall write nothing but what my Beloved suggests to me…» p. 75. «Many times my God rebukes me because I did not write what I saw and experienced. Today I want, as best I can, in haste, to write (in order to obey) what I saw in the first days of August»… Fascicle 5 part II p. 37: «Since the month of April I have not been able to write a line. Now in this night already far advanced, what shall I do? Lie down, for I was told not to stay up, and obey my good, who for several days has been telling me to write, and when? if not this night; by day it is difficult»… Fascicle No. 2 =Meditation for all the days of Lent 1864 in Genoa= says: «Finding in my papers certain pieces of sheets written with meditations, I truly wanted to tear them up, but a strong impulse drove me to copy them as best I could, being accustomed to let myself be led, and when I feel that something holds me back and makes resistance within me according to the movement, I care for nothing else»…

The letters, for the most part, are sent to the Sisters of the Institute, especially to the Visitors and Superiors of either Provinces or Houses, for the good government of her religious Family; they are full of prudent and wise dispositions and counsels. Among the letters there are some to Their Eminences the Cardinals of the H.R.C., to Bishops, Priests, Religious and very distinguished Seculars. In many shine the gravity, piety, humility of the S.G. and also the fortitude to preserve religious discipline and defend the rights of the Sisters and of the Institute. Which is no wonder, since she herself testifies that God at times dictated the letters. Thus in fascicle No. 4 p. II p. 15 she says: «I have letters to write; since I am an ignorant beast, He dictates to me what I must say; I am in the presence of persons with whom matters of interest to the work are treated; one thing happens in me: it seems that within me there is a person who speaks for me, because the words come out of me without my knowing what I say; I feel and understand that they are not mine, because I would not be capable of saying them. My God, He makes the most ignorant of creatures speak, makes her act, such as I am…» and more openly she writes in Fascicle No. 5 p. IV p. 111 year 1885: «After Holy Communion my good dictated to me a letter that I had to write to a Cardinal, and this He did many times; I would never have thought of doing that act of duty, or else because His work required it for its own good. Behold, He warned me: you will do this and that; so many times He dictated letters to the Administrations and, how I was to do it, He showed me the advantage that would derive from it. Have I not reason to say that I have never done anything, and to be ashamed and feel myself blush when they tell me something, because poor people think I am good? Ah! yes, at spoiling, that indeed, because many times I do not understand well and I am so ignorant that I cannot grasp the sublimity of the speaking of my Dear Master. Because of my ignorance my good must even stoop to dictate the letters to me. Ah! what I feel when He dictates and I see and hear such beautiful things! Ah! my Love, my Sweet Master…».

The letters called circulars, which the S.G. wrote each year and on the occasion of some event, are official documents, whose purpose is to communicate to all the Sisters of the Institute the more notable matters pertaining to the religious family, to correct public defects and to exhort the Sisters, especially the Superiors, to a stricter regular observance.

The talks =Conferences=, like the meditations, are brief, easy and pious discourses given to the Sisters, especially to the Novices and younger postulants, exhorting them to the practice of the virtues of humility, holy prayer and regular observance.

The autograph manuscripts divided into nine fascicles seem to me to be the Memoirs themselves reworked in better order and with a certain unity. The Servant of God shows the harder struggles endured to carry out the will of God who called her to labor in the vineyard or field of the Lord, and she discloses the graces and consolations that gladdened her soul, and the heavenly help she received to overcome all difficulties and to defeat the enemies who strove to hinder the work of the Lord. In the discourse she speaks in figurative sense of the field and the vineyard, to cultivate which the Lord sends his servant, that she may seek and hire many workers and good laborers, so that the uncultivated field may be converted into a chosen vineyard and a fertile and most pleasant garden.

The notes and annotations written by the Servant of God are nothing other than signs to refresh the memory of things done and to be done.

Having shown the number of the writings, the argument and the purpose of the author, I now come to my opinion. I judge that in those writings there is contained no error against the faith and good morals, nor is any doctrine found foreign to the common sense and custom of the Church.

Rather, there shine forth the singular humility of the S.G., her great prudence, her charity in caring for the sick; but the virtue which from the writings appears more proper to the S.G. is Love for Christ Crucified; she burned with desire to suffer with Christ… «My Dear Crucifix!»… Behold the words which she always had in her heart and on her lips. In Fascicle No. 5 p. I p. 51 she writes thus: «Oh! how sweet it is to suffer a thousand hells with Jesus. Together with Jesus, my sweet good, the most atrocious pains become so sweet that it does not seem in the least to suffer…». And in Fasc. 62 leaf 17, by obedience, she recounts the more rigorous penances imposed on her, the vigils, fasts, scourgings and every kind of austerities, and says: «Obedience! although I find much repugnance, yet I shall obey»… she narrates her more cruel mortifications, and continues: «My Love, you know that I want, therefore hear me, for I shall do all you wish, may your will be accomplished in me… My Love, consume me, for I feel myself burning, oh! love, whoever lives of you has nothing to desire, only you, treasure of every good!…». And it is to be noted that the S.G., in the year 1858, among the visions and ecstasies with which she was consoled, saw or came to know that her name was written in the book of the saints and that her sins had been blotted out by the blood of J.C. Behold her words: Fasc. No. 1 p. I p. 5: «At other times I was absorbed and as in colloquy I remained with my Jesus; many things He taught me. For a long time at the end of this colloquy He made me see two books which were held by two Angels each book; one far more beautiful and not so thick, in it were written certain names and then Saints; at the end was my name written large, and then Saint, written clearly; in the other, which was thick, were my sins, more than half was written and all cancelled I saw them with the blood of my dear Redeemer, and at the end of the writing again, as above, my name and P.S.…».

Although the writings of the S.G., taken in general, are judged worthy of praise, yet there are a few things to be observed, since the Code of c.l. Can. 2068 § 1 prescribes that the revisers of writings, together with the judgment on doctrine, inform in some general way also what character, what habit of virtues or defects appear from the writings to have been proper to the Servant of God. Now, from what has been said the proper virtue of the Servant of God Sister Anna Rosa Gattorno is evident; I shall now speak of the defect found in the writings.

Can. 2068 § 1 prescribes that the revisers of writings, together with the judgment on doctrine, inform in some general way also what character, what habit of virtues or defects appear from the writings to have been proper to the Servant of God. Now, from what has been said the proper virtue of the Servant of God Sister Anna Rosa Gattorno is evident; I shall now speak of the defect found in the writings.

In the manuscript =Memoirs=, among the visions narrated by the S.G., I judge that some are subjective suggestions and persuasions rather than visions sent by God. For example, the vision of the approaching death of Pope Leo XIII is a true suggestion, so to speak. The H.F. Leo XIII, of h.m., died on 20 July of the year 1903. Whereas the S.G., in the year 1880, Fasc. 4 p. V p. 107, says: «Today only it was manifested to me that the death of the Pope is near and sweet, the successor will be wholly for the Daughters of St. Anne!!». Afterwards, in the year 1887, fasc. 9 p. II p. 9, she writes: «Yesterday I saw Pope Leo XIII who stood on top of a rose-bush flowering with white roses. There were very many; at the end of these roses there was a skull of a dead man, alas! his death draws near, and still more the Church always agitates me…». In Fasc. 42, letter 352 sent to His Eminence Lord Granito di Belmonte, now His Eminence Cardinal Dean of the H.C., the Servant of God narrates the same vision, saying: «I would like a promise, and it is that you speak to no living creature of what I communicate to you. My God! You will forgive me if I dare say, also to the confessor, no one, how much pain this does not bring me. I saw Pope Leo XIII on top of a great rose-bush all in flower and they were white roses, a great cascade, and almost at the end of it inside the bush a skull of a dead man, and then arid and dry a piece of ground. As regards the P.G., there is no longer any danger of having to speak; my pure confession and nothing more, this consists, as I told you the other day, and then it is a matter of little time; as regards speaking of one or another, there is no danger; on this point my God asks of me a strange doing and feeling, but even at the cost of the greatest suffering, never can the secrets, the confidences come out of me…».

It is certainly remarkable that the S.G. asks of His Eminence Di Belmonte the promise to keep absolute silence and affirms that nothing is to be manifested to her confessor, indeed that she cannot even manifest it; whereas of a similar and far more singular vision she writes spontaneously in letter 108 fasc. 43 of 1890 to Emilia Settimo di Fitalia, adorned with a noble principality =Princess of Fitalia=, Rome 19.2.90: «Dear daughter. How are you? yesterday, last day of carnival, at night, before this g.n. possessed (sic), you should have been in a hole to see the lot of the devils who were in my room: at two after midnight, in the two bones of the arms, at the joint, a pain that made me faint; it seemed that a man's fist was dislocating my kneecap! And it was this monster who was doing this to me; but resigned I set to meditating, and so I continued until 4 in the morning. This having ceased, behold a revolution of devils running one behind another; they were big, of a loathsome shape, broad of body and as if they had an infinity of stuff to carry; it was well understood that it was to turn upside down precious families and other religious. I assure you that on one side, from the impression they left me, I suffered much, but on the other it was laughable. One passed in the figure of Leo XIII dying and disfigured, another a woman who was quarreling, at last a skeleton, another with moustaches (Crispi) it seemed to me, and this majestic; you will say it was a potpourri of everything. Did you not laugh?… See, by day he sleeps, stays hidden because he is so ugly, he is ashamed to be seen, what do you say?…».

Against this manifestation I can also cite what the S.G. writes in Fasc. 1 p. I p. 30: «It must be noted that for the first grace I asked of my Love, that is, not to permit that any earthly creature should ever notice that I have the least thing that could be believed good, in a word that everything be hidden from the eyes of men, and my good promised it to me, that no one would ever have seen or known anything of me!!».

Nor is the fact narrated in Fascicle 5 p. III p. 77 year 1884 to be passed over in silence: «I went to the Vatican where the Holy Father was expected to have us make Holy Communion and through indisposition he did not come, and instead the Cardinal Secretary of State had us make it…» p. 85. «In the union this morning with his side, which I did not feel, my God, Beloved Love, made me understand what the Pope who will succeed this one will be like. Oh! terrible sight!!! but it will last little. The Other will be a Saint and will do great things for our Catholic Church! and this one, I saw him pretending to be holy and promising… but all pretenses! to reach his aim. But Dear Jesus will permit it for His just ends…».

It is not sufficiently clear of what person she speaks; whoever it may be, the writing offends against the virtue of charity. Even supposing that the S.G., by an extraordinary way, truly knew the simulation of the person, it would not be lawful to commit it to writing, though the writing be for private use, unless there were a mandate or divine permission, which is not sufficiently established nor can we prove.

These are the defects that appear in the writings of the S.G.; I judge, however, that these and other matters of lesser moment present nothing that is not consonant with the orthodox faith or good morals or the sound and pure doctrine of Holy Church.

The judgment on the writings of the S.G. which were handed to me having been pronounced, I cannot complete the work without remarking on something truly singular. Among the writings which I received there are nine fascicles, autographs of the S.G., designated under No. 5° of this report; now, in these autographs nothing at all is said as to whether they were written to be published or for private use only, whereas in the List of the Writings of the S.G. kept in the Chancery of the S.R.C. the same autographs are thus entered under No. 69: Manuscripts of the book written by the Servant of God in 9 notebooks, which was printed with the title «Labors and Consolations of the soul on the way of perfection».

It is indeed true that the aforesaid book was published in print, Palermo, year 1897. Since I did not find this book among the writings entrusted to me, the judgment pronounced by me is confined to the autographs only. What more shall I say? in my opinion the manuscripts in question, as they exist, cannot be made public, both because of defect of literary form, for, as was said in this report, they present a continuous writing without any division into chapters, articles, etc., and because of the style of the whole writing, most difficult to grasp; for the Servant of God always speaks metaphorically of the labor done by her in the field or vineyard of the Lord, which properly seems to be the Religious Institute of which she herself is Foundress.

Why then is this printed work not among the writings handed to the Reviser? A concealment made deceitfully may be suspected. Certainly a book made public must be judged more severely than an autograph written only for private use; especially in our case, for it concerns the Foundress of a Religious Institute of Sisters, who followed her, the General Superior, with greatest love and veneration as Mother; and therefore with the danger of not rightly understanding the figurative sense of the book or of making false interpretations of it.

RO»

These are the things which I judged I ought to report in the Lord to Your Most Reverend Eminence, with all due reverence, in order to fulfill the charge received. All this I submit to the better and wiser judgment of Y.E.

Rome, 16 December 1931

FR. APOLLINARIS PEREZ

Theologian-Censor

2. Opinion of the Most Rev. Fr. Stefano Ignudi OFMC, Second Censor of the writings of the Servant of God, dated 8 February 1934.

IN THE NAME OF THE LORD

By commission of the Holy Congregation of Rites, for the space of two years I had frequent and diligent care to examine the Writings of the Servant of God Anna Rosa Gattorno, for the purpose of treating her Cause of Beatification and Canonization.

According to the order laid down in the Work On the Canonization of Saints (Lib. II, Chap. 27), I report the following, in conscience.

E kO

DIVISION OF THE WRITINGS OF THE S.G.

The Writings of the Servant of God submitted for examination are listed in the Document 13 attached to them, composed of eight typewritten pages.

They are contained in 80 Fascicles; and by reason of subject they can be distributed in the following order:

I. Memoirs of the Servant of God, on the foundation of the Institute of the Daughters of

St. Anne and on her own life (Fascicles 1, 2, 3, 4, 5,

7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 14).

II. Autograph Writing, consisting of 9 notebooks (quaderni), printed

with the title: Labors and Consolations of the soul on the Way of

Perfection (Fascicle 69).

III. Letters (Fascicles 15 to 61; 63 to 68; 70 to 74; 77, 79, 80). IV. Addresses, Meditations, Annotations (notes, jottings) (Fas-

cicles 6, 13, 62, 76, 78).

V. Rules, Constitutions for use of the Institute of the Daughters of St. Anne;

Method of assisting the sick (Fascicle 75).

PURPOSE OF THE SERVANT OF GOD

In writing the Memoirs on her own life she was led by the precept and obedience of the directors of her spiritual life, as is evident to the reader.

As to the Memoirs on the foundation of the Institute of the Daughters of St. Anne, she intended to preserve and hand down historically the facts that pertain to it.

As to the nine booklets (quaderni), which were afterwards printed, she wished to narrate, under the figure of a cultivator of the mystical Vineyard, the history of several houses founded by her.

Rules, Constitutions, Addresses, Meditations, Letters: all these refer to the care, government, administration of the Institute founded by her.

There do not seem to be any Writings that do not pertain to this end, namely the foundation and existence of the Institute.

o *

PROPOSITIONS WORTHY OF CENSURE «STRICTE INTELLECTA» IN THE WRITINGS OF THE S.G. NOT FOUND: a few expressions are certainly found which, considered by the manner of speaking of theologians, are less exact. I noted the following; which, however, can be rightly understood and reformed, certainly according to the mind of the Servant of God.

Fascicle II, p. 123 (year 1864): she speaks of a meditation of hers: «the thought of the meditation was very lively, and united to the union I cannot say apostatic (that is, hypostatic) BECAUSE I was perfectly in full power to feel materially and reason». Therefore by hypostatic union she means the highest union with God, by infused contemplation, with abstraction from the senses and from the discursive act of the intellect.

The same recurs, certainly in the same sense, two other times: namely:

Fascicle 12; Notebook 23 (1891-92); p. 26: «… I meditated… so vividly that I do not know whether I was in reality with my God, or only in the hypostatic union, thus to see and feel oneself».

p. 846

Fascicle 69; Notebook 7 (1892); p. 4: «in those sufferings I enjoyed a great consolation, it was the apostatic (that is, hypostatic) union with my God».

Fascicle 62, No. 4: Consideration on the heart that receives the essence of the love of Jesus. To the soul that will taste God «the greatnesses of down here will seem so worthless that she will flee from them every trace, to dwell forever in her center, which is God. The contemplation of the Most Holy Triad: first source, that everything is in Him; and only in the Divinity (that is, God in Substance), Triune in persons, etc.». A little below, she speaks to Jesus: «You are in this so most wretched Tabernacle: what annihilation was ever so great? a God part of the Divinity, indeed the very equality with the Father, because there is nothing in Him that is less than the Father». An unpolished language; but the mind of the S.G. is understood, which is always according to sound doctrine.

Fascicle 76: Meditations collected by the 1st Secretary (1870-71): Meditation II: On the Prayer and Agony in the Garden. - Something similar to the above is found; for she says to Jesus: «But why, my God, so great an annihilation, You who are a portion of that God (she means a Divine Person) who governs heaven and earth?».

In this same fascicle, I noticed in the Meditations that for sins of themselves venial she threatens Hell; but from the whole context and spirit of the meditation it is understood that if such things are held of little account, by a certain process of things for the worse they will lead to perdition. Nothing therefore contrary to moral discipline.

Fascicle 9: Notebook 8 (1889): p. 78: there are there three prayers or colloquies, to the three Divine Persons, to obtain some grace. The third colloquy, to the Holy Spirit, has a certain locution, doubtless uttered with simplicity of soul, but needing correction. It is thus:

«Holy Spirit, divine fire, by that outpouring by which at the conception of the Son of God in the womb of Mary Most Holy You cooperated in the great mystery of our Redemption, obtain from God the Father what our poor mother desires. 3 P. A. Glory».

«Here is my portrait but do not tell it to any, otherwise all will then want it. Every time you see it pray for me».

Fascicle 69. - There are 9 Notebooks: Manuscript of the book written by the Foundress Mother R. Gattorno. - It concerns the Memoirs, in which the S.G. speaks of her Foundations, in allegorical form. She herself is represented as a Pilgrim who goes either to establish new vineyards or to visit the fields, how they are cultivated: she narrates the difficulties, the hardships she suffered, or the consolations she experienced. Continually she meets the Shepherds, or they meet her. Of these Shepherds, some are good, but others adverse and bad. Under these figures of shepherds are understood without difficulty ecclesiastics of the secular or regular clergy, at times perhaps even Bishops.

Such Memoirs could be examined again and better: but they have already been examined and several times approved by Prelates and Theologians, both in the manuscript and in the printed copies.

In the printed copies, here and there several passages (pieces, excerpts) which are found in the Manuscript were omitted, and which deal especially with the said Shepherds.

My opinion is that in these Memoirs the facts be related only historically and simply, any injury to anyone removed: no Shepherd is indicated by proper name.

The Sisters (if need be) and some very high Prelate should be questioned: by whose order the said Memoirs were written, or by what impulse; and at whose instance they were printed (most certainly, indeed, given the perpetual and most profound humility of the S.G., they did not come to light in her lifetime).

As to sound doctrine, absolutely nothing is found in them to the contrary — the expression on the hypostatic union being reformed, as I said above —; as to the judgments or notes cast on certain Shepherds, I see nothing that would hinder proceeding further.

MOST REVEREND EMINENCE,

I have been charged with drawing up a vote on the «state of normality, or not, of the Servant of God Anna Rosa Gattorno, with express indication of its nature and its degree in relation to impairment of the personality»..

This problem arose because of the book «Labors and Consolations of the soul on the way of perfection», written by the Servant of God.

To be in a position to ascertain the psychic state of the author, it seemed to me my duty to inform myself about her life and work, as well as about the motives which led her to write the volume and about the circumstances of its publication.

I

LIFE AND WORKS OF THE SERVANT OF GOD

The life of the Servant of God has two well-distinct periods: from birth, 14 October 1831, to widowhood, 1858: from widowhood to death, 1900.

The first period appears normal, from the point of view of the question I have to answer: Rosa Gattorno was born of a very well-to-do family, had a good religious and cultural education, appears endowed with intelligence and strong will: balanced temperament. -

Spiritually she was well directed successively by two worthy priests.

She had three children from the marriage; the conjugal life had moments of grave difficulty, because of her husband's financial misfortunes; when he died he had again reached a high economic position.

During the financial difficulties, on the occasion of her husband's death and, barely three months later, of that of her son Francesco, Rosa Gattorno maintained a demeanor which showed not only the existence of a normal psychic life, but great strength of soul, dignity and a high degree of life of faith.

The second period concerns the birth of the Institute of the Daughters of St. Anne and its development, until Gattorno's death (1900). The Institute was born by the preeminent work of the Servant of God, but also with the encouragement and counsel of the Archbishop of Genoa Mons. Charvaz, of the Bishop of Piacenza Mons. Ranza and of the Supreme Pontiff Pius IX himself.

Here a reflection at once imposes itself: personalities of such high level do not commit themselves personally in counseling and encouraging a Foundress if she, as regards spiritual gifts, human capacities and balance, does not offer guarantees of reliability. The facts confirm that the trust granted her was deserved: she founds the Institute in 1866; when she dies in 1900 the Institute counts 309 houses in Italy, 49 abroad; the Sisters are more than 4,000.

If one considers the historical period in which she worked (exactly when in Italy the Government decreed the suppression of the religious Orders and Congregations), if one bears in mind how much organizational and financial commitment the foundation of more than 300 religious houses with their attached works (schools, nurseries, hospitals, shelters etc.) demands, one cannot but conclude that whoever presides over the concrete realization of all this truly possesses gifts of intelligence, of will, of balance at an undoubtedly superior level.

A psychopath cannot bring into being so imposing a work in barely 34 years.

In fact, works of such magnitude are not exempt from objective difficulties of various kinds and from adversities arising from interested persons: Anna Rosa Gattorno had to face particularly difficult and painful moments, which here it is not the case to specify: for our purpose it is enough to observe that she always reacted in a composed manner: no rancor, no depressive crises, but the conscious and serene attitude of one who suffers for a higher end.

Illness and death constitute a further element of judgment: physical evil did not affect her psychic life negatively: the sufferings were accepted and willingly offered to the Lord.

The last days she lived on earth, the conscious way in which she received the sacraments, the awareness and serene acceptance of death, indicate that Anna Rosa Gattorno, from the psychic point of view, was normal. From the spiritual point of view and of the exer-

II

HOW AND WHY THE VOLUME «LABORS AND CONSOLATIONS…» WAS PUBLISHED

The Servant of God received continual urgings from the future Cardinal Granito di Belmonte, from Princess Fitalia and from the Sisters to write the history of the Institute, which had flowered and developed in a surprising way;

Gattorno, yielding to the affectionate pressures, wrote some notebooks, without thinking in the least of printing;

having to write the history of the many foundations (309 houses in Italy alone), she had to suffer much, because many were the difficulties and misunderstandings she had to face and overcome;

by an act of high charity, she wished to keep silent the names of the persons who for her were the cause of unjustified persecutions and great pains; she wished to keep silent also the names of the places where the events took place, because, by revealing them, it would have been easy to trace the persons: she kept a conscious, generous silence also on the concrete facts and on the circumstances that accompanied them, and this always with the praiseworthy aim of not revealing the authors of her pains; moreover Cardinal Granito di Belmonte makes known that Mother Gattorno consciously used allegorical language, also with the precise aim of hiding, out of humility, the part she had in the birth and development of the Institute.

It is useful to adduce here some example of the manner of expression

_

of the Servant of God: when she wishes to describe the foundation of new houses, she speaks of «fields of the Lord to be cultivated»; when she wishes to highlight the good received from Superiors, she speaks of «good shepherds»; when, on the other hand, she noted that some of these did not give themselves wholly to pastoral work, but worried more about themselves than about souls, the Servant of God qualifies them as «indolent, slothful shepherds» etc.

Not infrequently, when she saw that some difficulties arose suddenly, without apparent explanations, her mind went to the enemy of every good, the devil, and she speaks of «ferocious lions», of «vultures» or of other animals that invaded the fields of the Lord to destroy them. The sisters are always depicted as «workers» whom God sends into his fields: some are zealous, others lukewarm; some let themselves be swayed by shepherds not upright; others, after a period of enthusiastic work, are seized by laziness and in a short time change a flowering garden into a field full of weeds.

The whole volume is written in this kind of symbolic language.

To be objective, I report the facts in the words of the protagonists: Cardinal Granito di Belmonte expressed himself thus in his deposition:

«I had exhorted the Servant of God to write the history of the foundation; but she, from continual fear of coming out of her shadow, seemed to me not much disposed to consent. Then pressures were added from other persons; among these from Princess di Fitalia, great admirer of the Servant of God and benefactress of her Institute.

So the Servant of God found herself obliged to yield. She set to work and handed a writing to Princess di Fitalia, who, aided by Cardinal Guarino Archbishop of Messina and by Canon Pennino of the same Cathedral, both masters of the spirit, had it published. In the edition of the said manuscript, preceded by two letters of praise for the work addressed to the Princess, they placed on the frontispiece the title, in my view unfortunately wrong: “Labors and Consolations of the soul on the way of perfection described by a Servant of God”, and it bore the approval of the ecclesiastical authority of Palermo.

I said that the title was unfortunately wrong, because in the reading which I made recently of the printed text I ascertained that it was nothing other than the true history of the foundation and development of the Institute of the Daughters of St. Anne, which the Servant of God had artfully wished to hide under figures, allegories and other things, so that the mission she had had in this fact of the foundation would not come to be known. I was able to ascertain with certainty what I have said, because I was perfectly aware of the facts reported in that book in allegorical form. Which facts were then confirmed to me by the religious who were part of them or otherwise had knowledge of them *. The book with such a wrong ti-

From the two documents it emerges that the volume was approved several times by ecclesiastical authority, namely:

— by the Most Rev. Mons. Gonfalonieri, Canon, Reviser, Theologian of the Florentine Curia;
