— by His Em. Guarino, Archbishop of Messina;

— by Canon Pennino, Reviser of the Palermo Curia;

— again by the same Palermo Curia, when the volume was reprinted in Palermo.

Had no confusion been made between the history of the Institute and the history of a soul, nothing would have happened, in the sense that the volume would not have been withdrawn from circulation.

There exist then two important letters, both for the authority of those who wrote them and for their content.

The first letter, addressed to Princess di Fitalia, is from Cardinal Guarino, Archbishop of Messina, and bears the date of 22 April 1894: the Most Eminent Archbishop's statements are highly laudatory and set out the grounds of his praise.

The second letter is from Theol. Can. A. Pennino and was written in Palermo dated November 1897, without specification of the day: the addressee is again Princess Emilia di Fitalia.

Canon Pennino expresses a twofold judgment: first of all he notes that in the work «there is nothing that could in the least offend faith and morals» (cf. Labors and Consolations of the soul on the way of perfection, Palermo 1897, p. VII).

Secondly he highlights that in the work written by the Servant of God there are many teachings «that can result in the edification and guidance of souls» (ibidem).

In it are found documents «very effective for making virtues appreciated, loved, practiced» (ibid., pp. VI-VII).

These two authoritative letters give the work of the Servant of God a more than sufficient guarantee of integrity of doctrine, both from the dogmatic and the moral point of view.

In any case the printed volume was a cause of great pain for the Servant of God while she was alive, and for the Cause, which received a «reponatur».

This, however, was the fruit of a great misunderstanding, which was well brought out by Cardinal Granito di Belmonte: whoever examined the volume thought that it described the history of a soul, that is, the spiritual, intimate journey of the Servant of God. And precisely here lies the great blunder: the volume has as its object the history of the new Institute founded by Gattorno: which is profoundly different.

p. 865

To apply to the spiritual life, reserved and intimate by its nature, what is instead written about the history of an Institute of 4,000 persons and of more than 309 houses is to falsify (even if involuntarily), in this case, facts and circumstances.

I also wished to investigate how the volume brought annoyances and sorrows to the Servant of God, because it was examined by the Holy Office and led to the «reponatur» imposed on the Cause: this supplementary investigation became necessary because data and elements useful for the judgment asked of me by the Sacred Congregation could emerge from it.

One fact emerges above all and of determining importance: someone spread the rumor that the Servant of God — who had been joined in marriage and had had three children from it — used the Institute's money in favor of them.

The accusation was grave and there was an apostolic visit which lasted from 1898 to 1903: it must be borne in mind that Anna Rosa Gattorno died in 1900.

The visit concluded with a result fully favorable to the Foundress; for her, however, it was a cause of profound bitterness, borne with humility and fortitude. Among other things, the Apostolic Visitor H. E. Mons. Domenico Serafini, later Cardinal, had in hand the volume «Labors and Consolations» and, while recognizing that it contained nothing condemnable, ordered that it be withdrawn from circulation.

Meanwhile the son-in-law of the Servant of God, who had married her daughter Carlotta, had the volume reach the Holy Office; he was opposed to the Foundress, because he demanded from Mother Gattorno large sums which she refused him: hence his gesture of having the volume reach the Holy Office.

We officially do not know exactly the reason why the Holy Office imposed a «reponatur» on the Cause: from the action taken by His Eminence Cardinal Granito Pignatelli di Belmonte (cf. his deposition at the process), it is easy to deduce that the attitude of the Holy Office was determined by the misunderstanding I have already mentioned: the volume «Labors and Consolations etc.» does not describe the history of a soul, but the birth and development of an Institute (cf. File «Apostolic Visit» 1898-1903, pp. 1-20, Archive of the General Seat).

p. 866

After this fundamental clarification it is easier to examine the individual elements of judgment that make it possible to answer the question put to me.

II

COMPARATIVE EXAMINATION OF THE VOLUME «LABORS AND CONSOLATIONS»

AND THE OTHER WRITINGS OF THE SERVANT OF GOD

I thought it opportune to take up, even if briefly, this argument too, in order to be in a position to present a well-founded conclusion.

These are the writings:

Memoirs written at the urging of His Most Eminent Cardinal Granito di Belmonte: they run from 1858 to 1893 (10 fascicles: Mmm 1 to 10);

Notes for conferences: 1888-1898 (3 fascicles: Mmm 11, 12, 13);

Various memoirs (2 fascicles: Mmm 14, 15), in total 3,637 pages.

There are then 8,487 letters handed over to the Holy Congregation (MaL; MI): of these letters fully 6,464 concern the Foundress's relations with her Sisters.

It is clear that I could not examine all this material: an examination, however, even if partial, of the Memoirs and of the letters offers a more than sufficient foundation for giving a reasoned judgment on the psychology of the writer.

In the Memoirs Anna Rosa Gattorno sets out both her own spiritual life and what she put into action for the foundation and development of the Institute: it was Cardinal Granito di Belmonte who encouraged her to write: in his deposition the Most Eminent witness expresses himself thus about these writings:

«For me they have a real value of truth, by reason of the serious, frank, unexalted and simple character of the Servant of God. In the contact I had with the Servant of God I became convinced that she was wholly alien to any artifice, to hiding second intentions, and I always knew her frank, upright, loyal» (Roman Process, vol. I, Session XV, fols. 136-137).

p. 867

«In reality the prose is simple, the phrasing limpid, quite different from the way she expresses herself in the volume “Labors and Consolations…”».

The letters, then, constitute a fine term of comparison: the epistolary dialogue with the Daughters is free of any artifice, maternal, concrete, edifying. The number of the letters arouses no wonder: the foundation of 358 houses, in Italy and abroad, the great administrative and disciplinary problems that had to be faced and resolved, the government of more than 4,000 Sisters imposed a dense correspondence.

The content of the letters and the manner of expression show a clear mind, a spirit that looked to the concrete and the essential. The balance, the sense of the supernatural, the concern for the spiritual good of the persons she addressed emerge with evidence.

In the Roman Process some recipients of the letters in question spoke: their judgment is more than positive and unanimous, moreover: besides Cardinal Granito di Belmonte, already cited, cf. Canon Pietro Tosti, vol. VIII, session CCXVIII, fol. 1672; Sister Vittoria Archetti, vol. II, session XLVII, fol. 368; Sister Santina Solenghi, vol. VI, session CXLII, fol. 1084; Sister Ancilla Briccoli, vol. VII, session CLXXXVI, fol. 1440; Sister Amante La Barbera, vol. XII, session CCCLIII, fol. 2751.

It is not my task to bring to light the positive aspects in all these writings: certain it is that from them no indication emerges that would allow doubt about the psychic balance of the author.

IV

INTERNAL CRITERIA EMERGING FROM THE WRITINGS OF THE SERVANT OF GOD,

FOR EXPRESSING A JUDGMENT ON HER PSYCHIC STATE

OF THE SAME

Our aim is to ascertain the state of psychic normality, or not, of the Servant of God: in order to reach conclusions founded on reality, as can emerge from the careful examination of all the elements useful for expressing a judgment on the psychic integrity of the Servant of God, from the intellective-volitive and, consequently, spiritual and moral point of view, it seemed to me my duty to dwell attention on two essential sources:

1. on the examination of what appears from the writings, the words, the actions of Mother Anna Rosa Gattorno;

2. on what eyewitnesses have narrated concerning her.

This twofold aspect of my examination had as its object the behavior of the Servant of God as regards the virtue of charity, in its aspect toward God and toward the brethren, as well as with regard to all the virtues, theological, cardinal and related.

Charity toward God

Regarding God, thus she expresses herself:

._ «I beg you to speak to me only of the greatnesses of God and of his omnipotence and mercy. These three matters alone are of great satisfaction to me, both in hearing them spoken of and in stopping to reason on them alone, because I found an immense greatness where the soul feeds and delights in its God against the same portion. Oh! the mind reasons and in such immensity has room to run without ever finding a stumbling that stops its reasoning; the intellect develops in the greatest cognitions of the soul in its relations with its God, that endless ocean of greatness, of power and mercy. The more the mind goes into it, the greater it sees the space, and ever new arguments unfold and the Majesty of a God is distinguished in broader proportions; and how the soul is always subject to Him and how it groans painfully when, through the darkness in which it sees itself wrapped on account of sin, it feels itself sent away by Him» (Labors and Consolations, p. 313).

«In the love of God is all the divine essence and it has no limits nor end; that of creatures is fallacious and soon vanishes, withers like the rose plucked from the plant which, set in the sun, sees in the open air the disillusion of the fleeting things of earth. But the love of my God, Master and Lord, flames ever more in the heart of creatures and finally with its rays ravishes and in His most sweet divine ether consumes. Oh! yes, Love!» (Ibid., p. 252).

«Tell me still something of my God, to see whom I feel so much ardor! My thirsting soul seeks Him everywhere and burns with strong desire to speak to Him and to unite with Him as its only center. In His will your soul finds Him again. Oh! too sweet it is to do it and in everything to find a reverse to one's own will, when this is still possessed» (Ibid., p. 100).

p. 869

«My Love, I am ready for everything so that Your Divine will be satisfied» (Ibid., pp. 15-16).

«Oh my Eternal Father! From you I have everything, for You I do everything, my only being you are» (Memoirs vol. 6, p. 274; cf. also p. 213).

«How can I do to make You known to all the world? Oh! how many there are who do not know You, and those who have known You flee You for never having seen You. I would like to run everywhere and cry out loud that all might come to love You» (Memoirs vol. 1, p. 36).

Cardinal Granito di Belmonte, in his sworn deposition, confirms with his authority this ardent love of the Servant of God toward the Most High:

«Most ardent was her love toward God, whom she always guarded herself, with every solicitude, from displeasing even with the lightest fault… By her charity she expiated with harsh penance her presumed faults and those of others so that the wrath of the Lord might be calmed. In conversing with her I always had to note her great love toward God, although she did nothing to manifest it to me, being reserved in her words, in her bearing, in every act of hers. This reserve of hers was constant with all and she made her hiddenness a continual object of her prayer, as was said, so that no one could have known what flame of charity burned in her heart had he not known the continuity of her acts and the results of her works… Her charity toward God moved her in the conferences to her Religious when she instructed them on prayer and exhorted them to regular discipline, interpreting successively all the points of the rule. In a word, God was the one who occupied her whole heart» (Card. Granito di Belmonte, Roman Process, vol. I, Sess. XII, fol. 112).

Devotion to the Crucified

Love toward Jesus Crucified, to cancel the sins of all men, of all times, had in her manifestations of strong understanding, which the Servant of God wished to bring down into the daily practice of her life.

The volume «Labors and Consolations etc.», written during the last period of her life, is a limpid testimony of it:

«My Crucifix led me along a road and on it I fell ill. He was my physician, in weariness He gave me strength. Many times I slipped on the narrow path and He sustained me, so that I would not fall from the crags…» (p. 3).

«My Crucifix! I was very deformed and He with His grace made me beautiful, adorning me with His graces: He stripped me of the old man, and of a gentle creature I remained clothed…» (Ibid., p. 3).

«My Crucifix has exchanged my will for His, and it is infinitely sweet and pleasant not to possess it. Oh, how it would have rebelled, had He not nailed it, while yet it remains always free» (Ibid., p. 4).

Rose's Crucifix is involved in her story, living, active:

«Silent I stayed with my mind leaning on the side of my Crucifix, I felt that it was gathering strength and fine cognitions for the journey that I still had to make» (Ibid., p. 73).

He taught her:

«My Crucifix! He taught me to suffer and, like the honey of the bees, enclosed in those precious combs, He kept for me the suffering which was changed into sweetness. From time to time He gave me some of this humor to taste, and with sublime lessons made me understand how such exquisiteness was drawn from suffering, while nature was rebellious to it» (Ibid., p. 3).

«Ah! My Love, what do You want? I know no more what to give You, because all is Yours: I have no more life, because it is Yours, because in all truth I can say that I no longer feel alive, but in Him I live. Oh dear Good!» (Memoirs, vol. 2, p. 76).

To her daughters she inculcated love for the Crucifix:

«Let us hold to the positive and strive greatly always to reason with the Crucifix before us, let us look at Him in all our actions whether they conform to His example, and then everything is annihilated and our sufferings become a fine nothing and less than nothing…

Cheer up, cheer up, for Jesus likes those who suffer, whoever does not want to suffer does not want to love» (Letter to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, 16.1.1870).

The witnesses who were close to her report this love of hers for the Crucifix:

«She always spoke of the Crucifix with such transport and unction that it moved, especially when she gave conferences to the novices she always brought Him in. In tribulations and worries she withdrew to her room and prayed to her Crucifix, as could be understood from her exclamations: Ah! my Crucifix will think of everything. My Crucifix will guard His work! My Crucifix will succor His servant, and others like these» (Rom. Proc., vol. IX, Sess. CCLVI, fol. 1968 — Sr. A. Celsa Speranza —).

«When someone had recourse to her asking the help of her prayers she ordinarily answered: I will tell my Crucifix. In short, her Crucifix was for her the anchor for all the storms by which she was assailed. In a word, He was her all» (Card. Granito di Belmonte, Rom. Proc., vol. I, Sess. XI, fol. 102).

For reasons of space, I pass over what Anna Rosa Gattorno writes about her love for the Eternal Father (cf. Scattered Memoirs, pp. 345-1346; Memoirs, vol. I, p. 222; letter to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, of 1-6.1871).

No less expressive and profound are her words when she expresses what her soul feels toward the Holy Spirit (Memoirs, 1, p. 46; Memoirs, 4, pp. 8-9).

Devotion to the Most Holy Eucharist

Devotion to the Most Holy Eucharist had an undisputed pre-eminence in her life: Holy Communion and Holy Mass constituted the high point of each of her days:

«During Holy Mass I placed myself in that chalice, telling the Eternal Father to be pleased to look at me, because with the Blood of my love (Jesus) I was covered, soaked. On the altar of sacrifice there are two victims. Look upon us» (Memoirs 1, p. 210).

«While I was hearing Holy Mass and offering to the Eternal Father the Sacrifice of the Altar, a most vivid light appeared to me together with a voice that said to me: “This sacrifice of yourself in that chalice together with His beloved Son now pleases God, but it would please Him greatly that you offer yourself victim in all the sacrifices that are accomplished on the altar of the whole Catholic world” and at once I do not delay in doing it» (Memoirs 1, p. 143).

«Satiate me, for pity, with Your love, oh why do I not remain forever before Your tabernacle where, my Beloved, You are enclosed? what are 5-6 hours a day?… If men knew You, surely they would leave everything and be at the foot of Your altar to enjoy Your delights; but how can I make them understand» (Ibid., p. 46).

p. 872

«Strong as a giant because fortified by the Eucharistic food» (Labors and Consolations, p. 182).

«I am not worthy, my God, my Love, to receive You, but panting is my breast to possess You; the heart throbs to have You within. Behold the candles are lit and in a moment I shall possess You» (Ibid., p. 208).

«I threw myself at the foot of the Altar and with supreme desire awaited the coming of my God in me» (Ibid., p. 195).

Also on this moment of the spiritual life of the Servant of God we have the confirmation of serious and credible witnesses:

Her spiritual director:

«I am then so glad that you have been able to make Holy Communion every day; consider this a great gift from your spouse Jesus, who wants always to be united with you in this sacrament of love.

If I think of the great advantages that Holy Communion has brought you, I have good reason to tell you that the Lord loves you and loved you as a favorite. Believe me, since you have been frequenting it, you have become another from what you were before. Now you are wholly your Jesus'» (Letter of Don Firpo, 19-7-1861).

Three years later, precisely in 1864, this wise and holy priest, «first witness and depositary of so many graces» (as he himself asserts), would write to her again:

«You are no more; it is your spouse Jesus, your love, your all, who lives, who works in you. If then you are dead and no longer live, let him who works in you dispose all things; you, in His high and loving designs, must serve Him as nothing but a wretched instrument, as you are» (Letter of Don Firpo, 18-3-1864).

Cardinal Granito Pignatelli di Belmonte:

«Every day she received Communion and, to receive Communion, she subjected herself to whatever sacrifice it cost her. Traveling, even if she arrived at noon at her destination she was not found to have broken the fast, and her first thought was to go and make Communion. For this purpose she interrupted, if necessary, the journey; if ill, she rose from bed only for this; and when in the last times, because of infirmity, she could no longer stay fasting, she sometimes availed herself of the permission to break it; yet such was her respect for the Church's prescriptions in this regard that very few times did she avail herself of such privilege, and she preferred to make the sacrifice in order to make Communion».

p. 873

.. «Ardent was her devotion to the Most Holy Sacrament, as already appears from what I have said about her Communions. She made visits to Him as frequent as she could, and sought, as she could, to extend His cult in her Institute» (Roman Process, vol. I, Session X, fol. 96).

Devotion to the Most Holy Mary

This is a characteristic of a soul that loves God, because God became man choosing this Mother.

And in reality, from childhood, Mother Rose was very devoted to Mary Immaculate. She belonged to the Association of the Daughters of Mary Immaculate of her city and later became its President; when it came to choosing the name of the Institute she was about to found, before the Lord manifested to her His precise will, she placed it under the title of the Immaculate.

She invoked Mary in her own needs and those of the work, but above all that she might help her on the way to God; to Her she entrusted her own children after the decisive audience of Pius IX, who commanded her to leave everything to follow the will of God.

«I laid everything at the feet of Mary Most Holy (the private perpetual vows of chastity and obedience) that she might make a gift of them to my good, Jesus, and beg Him to accept me as spouse» (Memoirs, 1, p. 3).

«Mary Most Holy, teach me to follow this holy Poverty as my dear Jesus, Your most beloved Son, desires» (Memoirs, 1, p. 20).

«I had put “Daughters of Mary Immaculate” (as title of the nascent Institute) because I was very much not only devoted but loving and wholly Mary's» (Memoirs 3, p. 335).

«O Mary, through you I am saved, through you I am religious; the fire of the love of your Son, Mary, with your hands many times you kindled in this heart of your Son. Oh joy! oh love! why do You not make me die of this?» (Memoirs 4, p. 121).

«Throwing myself prone on the ground, I cried out loud: Most powerful Sovereign, loose the sorrowful chains and carry me to my Crucifix» (Labors and Consolations, p. 8).

«I went to the feet of the Sorrowful Virgin in the Church of the Servites, where, after the death of their father, I had taken them and had consigned them to the Most Holy Virgin… Prostrate at the feet of this Sovereign and Queen of sorrows, in a flood of tears I said to her: — I must abandon my children, Your Son through His Vicar commands me. I feel torn by pain, because I bear them immense affection. You, my Mother, experienced the abandonment of Jesus. Merely to have lost Him for three days, what it cost You! Oh! my children, I do not know how to find strength to leave them! And where? And with whom? Alas, the pain is too strong! How unhappy I am! I am a mother and bear so much affection to my children! Mary, Mary, my Mother, what knife is this that pierces me to the marrow of my bones.

… My tears dried and in the Most Holy Virgin I gained peace, strength… I had very great consolations; and the Most Holy Virgin assured me that she would always be with me, and would keep my children as her own» (Memoirs, 3, pp. 340-342; ibid., 4, p. 120; Labors and Consolations, p. 111).

The witnesses fully confirm the filial and particular devotion of the Servant of God to the Most Holy Virgin (Sr. A. Camilla Valentini, Roman Process, vol. IX, Sess. CCLXIII, fols. 2021-2022; Cardinal Granito Pignatelli di Belmonte, ibid., vol. I, Sess. XI, fols. 101-103).

Devotion to St. Anne

The very fact that the definitive name given to the Institute she founded is that of Daughters of St. Anne shows how profound and heartfelt was the devotion of the Servant of God to the Mother of Mary Most Holy.

Love for St. Anne accompanied Mother Rose from the foundation of the Institute until death. She felt her continually present in the Work, invoked her in every need and exhorted her daughters to do so, saw in the observance of the Rules the way to honor St. Anne and to be truly her daughters.

«Love for St. Anne had so strongly penetrated me that all the listlessness I had vanished, and it became strong to such a point that in all my needs I invoked her and always found myself satisfied in Providence, in journeys, in everything; so impressed it remained that I always kept her before my eyes. Oh! my mama! I always exclaimed so» (Memoirs, 3, pp. 355-356).

«As soon as day broke my anxiety was to receive my Jesus and then to return to the working women to bring them the provision gathered, but a servant of a most distinguished noble Lady presents himself, and tells me that before leaving I should go to his mistress: “What can she want, I thought. After being fortified with the bread of angels I went there. What a marvel! She was gravely ill. Poor thing, she embraced me and said to me: “Do not let me die”. My God, if I were a good creature I would say I could hope in my prayers, but I at once blushed! What can I do, poor slave! Only serve you as best I can. I sought every means to serve her delicately, I remembered that the working women are always directed by St. Anne, and I proposed to her to make a great promise to this Mother, from whom I hoped much. This done I took her blessed water. Oh! prodigy of the great Holy Mother St. Anne! She was healed instantly. The promise was made at once and her daughters had other fields to cultivate» (Labors and Consolations, pp. 228-229).

According to the opinion of His Most Eminent Card. Granito Pignatelli di Belmonte, of Sr. A. Benedetta Carrega and of Sr. A. Celsa Speranza, the Servant of God alludes to the Marchioness Fanny Anguissola, born of the Dukes Visconti of Milan (cf. MLst - 1, study made by Card. Granito di Belmonte in collaboration with Mothers Benedetta and Celsa — see note 1, p. 5).

In the Foundress's letters to the Sisters, the heartfelt and constant devotion to St. Anne emerges with undeniable force.

«Dear daughters of St. Anne, Mother of you and of me, though unworthy indeed of being so, but daughter… Soon I shall be with you, I hope to find those dear creatures whom St. Anne desires observant of the Holy Rules, beginning from the morning on opening the eyes, until evening when overtaken by sleep» (to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa and Community of Sampierdarena, 12-4-1869).

«For charity keep well in memory what this your poor Mother told you and tells you: never tell lies, but let truth always be on your lips and you will live secure in the heart of St. Anne our Mother» (to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, 2-7-69).

«Daughters of St. Anne, Mother wholly ours, strive to deserve to be of the number of those who with transport of love will be able to say: wholly ours is the Mother; but one thing alone can estrange you and make you orphans: it is the transgression of your Rules…

Strive to be animated to the observance of your Rules and in this you will acquire true virtue and be able to say and deserve to be the daughters of St. Anne and say to her: you are our Mother, wholly ours» (to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni and Community of Piacenza, 25-8-69).

«I am convinced that if you have great faith, first in our Eternal Father, and then in St. Anne, you will see that in everything you will find yourself having what you need» (to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, 1-12-69).

p. 876

«I am sorry that you have not yet been able to pay any bill; well, the Holy Mother will pay them all» (to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, 3 July?70).

«Let us pray and have others pray that St. Anne, our Mother and the Immaculate's, change our heart» (to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, 27-4-71).

The witness Sr. A. Camilla Valentini speaks explicitly of this particular devotion of the Servant of God.

«St. Anne was considered by her as her Mother and the Institute's and therefore she called her the Holy Mother. To her sisters, when she saw that to obtain a grace they made various novenas to Our Lady under various titles, she said: “I am glad that you turn to Our Lady, but remember, however, that your Mother is St. Anne and that you must turn to her also. Do not forget her, do not put her in a corner”. In her conferences to the novices she said: “By honoring St. Anne you do no wrong at all to Our Lady, since it is Our Lady herself who wants her Mother honored”» (Roman Process, vol. IX, Sess. CCLXIII, fols. 2022 v.-2023).

Charity toward the neighbor

To ascertain the psychic balance of a subject, the study of his or her behavior toward the persons, of whatever rank and state, with whom she found herself in relation is of fundamental importance.

Here we have a vast range of persons, and therefore of reciprocal relations, with the Servant of God, which offer us a concrete and precise point of reference for reaching an objective conclusion on the personality of Anna Rosa Gattorno and for giving a well-founded judgment on the normality, or not, of her psychic state.

Here is the complete picture:

— neighbor in general;

— husband;

— children;

— relatives in general;

— Sisters;

— Superiors;

— children (little ones);

— the sick.

p. 877

Charity toward the neighbor reaches its highest and heroic degree when it is consciously employed toward adversaries and toward those who have been for us a cause of pain: the Servant of God, in this regard, affirms that she is happy to be unjustly condemned, and this only in order to imitate the Lord, who, before dying, forgave His executioners.

«My dear Crucifix, they condemned me only to give what they believed, but I was not condemned to death like You! They insulted me and I sought to imitate You in doing them good» (Labors and Consolations, p. 233).

And again:

«My Crucifix showed Himself beautiful to me, and greatly enjoyed what I suffered. Then my love for my persecutors grew; were it not that they offended God, I would have wished them doubled for me» (Ibid., p. 5).

«I prayed for my benefactress, for the one who had made me suffer that day, and thanked God for so great a grace as He had done me» (Ibid., p. 227).

One could go on, but it would be superfluous; one observation imposes itself: a person who consciously, that is, with clear orientation of the volitional act, decides not only to forgive adversaries who were authors of persecutions, adversities, sorrows, but prays for them and does them good, shows that she possesses a mental lucidity, an intact volitional capacity. From the moral and spiritual point of view there is no doubt that we are at the level of heroism in the exercise of charity.

We also note that the attitude of the Servant of God toward all persons was founded on charity:

«I would like to attract the whole world, give to all, feed all!… Oh if from my veins I could make gold flow out for the poor, do you know what I would do? From myself, vein by vein, I would draw it, until they were left dry!» (Letter to Sr. A. Celsa Speranza, no. 76, undated).

«Nothing seems to me that there can be of sweet on earth, nothing! only one thing one feels to taste: charity! Oh how much joy one feels in being able to benefit and do good, to set right in peace with God whoever is off the way! yes, in charity the soul rejoices, and in seeing the well-being of creatures it feels great pleasure; whatever pain the sacrifice cost, it always turns out a consolation to see a soul relieved» (Memoirs, 2, p. 127).

p. 878

The words of the Servant of God also have the counter-proof from those who had occasion to know her closely:

«Generosity has always been her dominant note and even now old women of her native shores remember their old benefactress and how much interest she took in imploring for whoever could obtain some relief» (Mr. Francesco Gattorno, Memoirs, p. 3).

«Of an eminently superior character with those she dealt with and without compromising her convictions, she had an innate tolerance that inspired respect and, though very young and in a period of political upheavals and in positions of finding herself in contact with the greatest thinkers and agitators, she was repaid with the utmost regard and her word was always effective on a par with her faith and her noble examples of sacrifice» (Mr. Francesco Gattorno, Memoirs, p. 8).

Husband

We know little of the married life of Anna Rosa Gattorno: she spoke of it rarely with a few intimate persons; but these testimonies are very significant.

«The husband died after having endured an illness of three months during which the Servant of God never left him either day or night. I remember that the Servant of God told me that the husband, even when he felt ill, did not want to omit reciting the Rosary every evening, and they spoke between them of spiritual things, as indeed had been done also in the preceding years, when the husband was in health.

Finally he died fortified with the Sacraments (…). Such a loss cost the heart of the Servant of God much, and, as soon as she ascertained the death, she fell into a swoon; yet her soul was always resigned to the will of God, as she herself told me. She had the soul of her husband aided with very many Masses, and every year on the anniversary of his death she had others celebrated» (Sr. A. Serafina Foglia, Roman Process, vol. III, Session LII, fol. 397; cf. also Sr. A. Celsa Speranza, ibid., vol. VI, Session CXLVII, fol. 1118).

Children

As regards the children, the conversation the Servant of God had with Pius IX is indicative: the objection she raised in begging the Supreme Pontiff to exempt her from the task of founding a new Institute had as its motive her duty and her mother's affection toward her children and her aged parents; she herself speaks of it: «I took heart and begged him (Archbishop Charvaz) that before trying to draw up a rule I wished to hear His Holiness Pius IX, because I hoped the Holy Father would take the obedience from me and would surely give such a charge to another… having two children and a father and mother very old to whom I was very attached, and could not do this of leaving them, no; my children, then, the mere thought of having to leave them was an agony, and I repeated to myself: no, it will never be, no (…). The audience was requested and was had on the 3rd of January at 5 in the afternoon, it was a private audience. Oh this day I shall never forget. My hopes vanished and a most bitter knife came to wound me strongly (…). I threw myself on the ground and weeping said to him: Holiness, I have two children, a father and a mother old, both, my children small. He answered me: It is no use: God so wills. Ah! no, Holiness! God, according to the Holy Gospel, will ask me account of my children — and I wept uncontrollably — I love them too much, I cannot leave them. Holiness, it is impossible (…). He said to me: God will think of your children, you think of God in His work. I rose and could hardly utter a word, I felt my breast breaking (…) perhaps I should not narrate certain particulars which only my God knew what they cost me and how much I suffered. How many times the temptation came to me to abandon everything and return to them (…) but the thought of acting against the will of God made me resist any martyrdom» (Memoirs, 3, pp. 328-329; cf. also: letter to her son Alessandro 10.8.1875; to the same while he was in America, undated, but certainly of 1876; to her daughter Carlotta, letter undated, but certainly written before 1874; to the same, letter of 13.8.1896).

When her son left for America, the Servant of God wrote:

«Today my son came to take leave, for he was leaving for America; the pain it caused me to think that I would not see him again gave me much grief, but most heart-rending was that in those lands of such depravity he might be lost, and if unhappily death should seize him, where would he go? For surely he would die without the comforts of Holy Church and, good Christian as he is, he would surely have forgotten my God, and then I would have lost him for an eternity. Oh sorrow! a creature who belongs to me will not die in the kiss of my God? shall I have to think that he will be a thorn in the heart of my Good? oh what have I done, I cannot bear so much pain! oh, my Love, a thousand deaths I would be willing to see him undergo, but as a Christian. All this I said weeping uncontrollably; when I finished uttering these last words my weeping stopped and I felt a calm within me; I resumed saying: My Love I promise You that if I have the fortune of seeing him die as a Christian I shall not shed a tear but shall absorb that sorrow come to me from Your most holy hands and happy to be able to hand him over that he be Yours for an eternity» (Memoirs, 2, pp. 97-98: cf. also the letter to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, of 25-9-1870).

p. 880

Also toward her other relatives the duties of charity and of justice were fulfilled in the most commendable manner: the persons directly concerned acknowledge it:

«At this point it is well to note the care she had for her mother in an illness and that which she began to give to her maternal grandmother, who came to live with her daughter on becoming a widow.

Her assistance to her, especially in the illness of 1850, the time of her death, is one of the proofs of her aptitude for giving care to the sick and with love consoling whoever suffers» (Memoirs of Mr. Francesco Gattorno 1903, p. 4).

«With her sweet look and convincing word she softened the commercial setbacks of her Father, industrious and of most honest character and honestly severe, and never departed from his counsels, repeating to all that a father's word is always sincere and one by which one may be sure of not being deceived» (Ibidem, p. 6).

«Love for her mother was always for her a religion and an assiduous labor to prevent, hide and mitigate everything that could, in that sensitive character and suffering constitution, cause the least displeasure and harm to her health.

And with the growing of the years she was no longer for her Mother only a daughter but a confidante to whom she revealed her every smallest thought, sure of finding another soul that sincerely shared with equal feeling her sorrows and her joys» (Ibid., pp. 6-7).

Sisters

She treated the Sisters with the affection of a mother: she directed, observed, counseled, exhorted, according to need, with a clear vision of the particular needs of each and with the anxiety to procure the spiritual good of all.

The vast correspondence that gathers the letters with the Sisters (fully 6,464 letters) constitutes a proof of tangible evidence for ascertaining her highly maternal and supernatural conduct toward the Sisters.

«My God, to you I consign these creatures whom You have entrusted to me: now I place them for all this time in the Heart of Your Son Jesus, and you cover them with heavenly dew, that they may be defended from every least encounter. In this retreat of the Heart of Jesus let them learn the true school of Your Divine Love» (Letter to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti 25-5-1871).

«Dear daughter, I assure you that this poor mother of yours has nothing else in her mind but your holiness and, unworthy as she is, never ceases to raise prayers to the Most High for your spiritual and temporal welfare» (Letter to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa and Sisters, 6-6-1869).

«For certain creatures Jesus is always on the Cross because they do not want to be on it, nor even to carry it; they leave it all on His Most Holy Shoulders. So I thought of having it given to me and of obtaining Tabor for them, so that… they become His true disciples» (Letter to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, 9-12-1869; cf. also: letter to S. A. Giovanna Bixio, of 20-2-1867).

She knew from long experience that the work of Superiors is little effective if their teachings and exhortations are not reinforced by their personal good example: she wrote, in fact:

«Oh! it is useless for a good captain to order his army to face the enemy, to take possession of the ground, if he himself does not go first exposing his breast to the grapeshot hurled by the enemy. So an overseer who wants her workers zealous and all intent on work, and who keep their mind and heart always turned to the Lord and master, must be the first who from dawn to dusk holds the spade in hand to furrow well all parts of the earth, so that in order the water of the grace of their Master may flow and water those souls well» (Labors and Consolations, p. 270).

Superiors

From the point of view of the proof concerning the virtues of the Servant of God, it is of determining importance to ascertain her conduct toward Superiors: charity, obedience, justice are involved in such conduct, and this offers determining elements of judgment.

But the conduct of a subject toward Superiors, involving directly intelligence, will, sensibility, orientation toward life, makes it possible to ascertain the state of her psychic balance.

Anna Rosa Gattorno, in her relations with Superiors, was animated by the supernatural spirit that orients her thinking and acting: a humble and obedient little sheep, who entrusts herself with absolute confidence to the shepherds assigned to her by Providence.

«An elegant shepherd, but very humble, approaches me and asks me news of the field, and with a charity of a true servant of my God he entered into various discourses… I begged him to be pleased to cast a glance at the fields where, as a slave, I had been sent to work… In his immense charity and goodness he made that path easy for me to travel. At every great rock I met, with his guidance I found myself relieved.

.. Thus assured I unfolded every theme however tangled it was, I entrusted to him the working out…» (Labors and Consolations, pp. 264-265).

«Sometimes I met the holy and charitable Shepherd who with charity and zeal helped me to surmount those stumbling blocks that lay along the path» (Labors and Consolations, p. 268).

This conduct of hers toward Superiors, in every circumstance, glad or less glad, was conscious, consistent and continuous: the witnesses who knew well the Servant of God's way of acting affirm it.

«At first my uncle the Cardinal came always every day or nearly to this Generalate House, then I do not know for what reasons he came no more here, not only that, but when the Servant of God went to the Cardinal, he no longer even received her except sometimes. This tension of relations began about a year before the death of my uncle, which occurred on 10 August 1899.

When he spoke to me of it afterward he showed himself annoyed, and did not want to hear it spoken of. The Servant of God, however, continued to go to the Cardinal, she sat in the antechamber like a poor woman, waiting to see whether the Cardinal would receive her. I never could perceive that she felt offended by this way of proceeding of the Cardinal toward her. She always had a good word to excuse him, and this without affectation and with all simplicity. She even redoubled her delicacies, her attentions toward the Cardinal, and it was manifest that she did not do it for so-called diplomatic ends. From that time I therefore began to conceive esteem for a woman of extraordinary virtue and to admire her.

I remember that in the end relations between them became good again and that my uncle heard the Servant of God spoken of again willingly» (Fr. Francesco Verga, Roman Process, vol. X, Session CCCXVI, fols. 2425 v.-2426).

«In Piacenza too difficulties were not lacking for the work of the Servant of God, difficulties which she met also from some of the local Clergy, who judged the foundation of new works inopportune. To overcome these difficulties the Servant of God had recourse to prayer, and here I wish to note that during her whole life, in the many times in which Ecclesiastics were for her and her Institute a cause of displeasure and of very strong opposition, the Servant of God had as a maxim never to make known to others what could give occasion to diminish the reputation of the same ecclesiastics, and I repeat again that her powerful means for succeeding in bringing remedy or making the truth known was prayer…

p. 883

The Servant of God was always very firm in the oversight and direction of the Institute, and this firmness she had to exercise, not infrequently and with devout submission, with Ecclesiastics and with Bishops. The Servant of God, in taking measures and dispositions in the direction of her Institute, in the most difficult circumstances always turned to Jesus Christ, to St. Anne and to her Holy Protectors, and did not carry out her steps and her measures except when she felt strongly assisted by supernatural aids. From this it followed that, when she was opposed by anyone, especially by Bishops or other Ecclesiastical Authorities, after having made her submissive observations, she did not oppose the measures demanded by others, since after some time these same persons had to recognize that the measures taken by the Servant of God were just and prudent, and had to follow them.

What I have now set forth I can affirm from personal experience, since, in the many years that I was in the direction of the Daughters of St. Anne in the House of Naples, it happened to me that I wished to take measures or to oppose some of the dispositions given by the Servant of God, and she never opposed my will, although she let me note that she did not agree with me. Time afterward, as I have indicated above, proved the Servant of God right» (Card. Granito Pignatelli di Belmonte, Roman Process, volume I, Sess. VI, fol. 64; Sess. VII, fol. 72).

Children

The experience of motherhood had marked forever Mother Rose's way of being, and she was particularly attentive and tender with children.

«If you knew the work that is here, surely you would not even write that she should come. As I already told you another time, we have begun to take the endangered girls who can hear, the Deaf-Mutes, the Endangered; I have no rest. Angiola is studying to pass as a certified teacher, so as to be able to take her course; soon we open the external schools» (Letter to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, 10 October 1867).

«I had the examinations of the little boys of the Death (house located in Via della Morte) who now number 148 and all ragged, true leftovers of prison. If you had seen! barefoot, one letting his shirt hang through a hole in his trousers… they did excellently well, and the listeners remained satisfied» (Letter to Fr. Agostino Donadio, 5-8-1872).

«I recommend to you the little girls and that you see they are well sheltered at night, so that they do not catch a cough; likewise the small ones, as to the cleaning of the vermin, and see that you change their shirt often, the head clean, school in the evening, otherwise they will lose all that they have already learned» (Letter to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, 25-9-1870).

«How much good is done in Ferrara! 189 girls taken from the school with the Jewish girls, and there they are taught to love and know the true God, the Church and her Vicar. What a consolation this is! Many of them we have admitted to Communion, what mercy of God for these foundlings, already we begin to take them into the house, drawing them from sin…» (Letter to Fr. Agostino Donadio, no. 46, probably of 1872).

«The Institute… professes the compassion of the heart of St. Anne… taking in the poor endangered girls to preserve them from losing innocence… they honor the care she had of the holy Immaculate Child and the zeal she will have had to see all the young girls of the world innocent» (Mother Anna Rosa Gattorno, Autograph manuscript: internal chronicle - aim of the Institute).

Her greatest concern regarding the smallest ones was to lead them to the Lord:

.. «How shall I be able to teach these mute creatures to love God and make Him known to them? Thinking thus I looked at them and felt the liveliest compassion…» (Labors and Consolations, p. 176; cf. again in the same sense: ibid., p. 20; pp. 48-49; pp. 124-125).

A witness certainly not suspect, given the milieu and circumstances of the time, is the Mayor of Piacenza, who officially thanked the Servant of God for what she did on behalf of the girls left orphans as a result of the cholera epidemic which had afflicted the city.

«Piacenza, 11 November 1867 — I have received the most gracious letter of Your Ladyship by which you offer free maintenance and free instruction and the rest in the refuge erected by you in this city for the girls left orphaned of parents on account of the cholera that afflicted this district in the current year. If such an offer causes no wonder in one who knows the spirit of charity which is the foundation of the pious and philanthropic institution erected by you, it does not however diminish in me the obligation of the most sincere gratitude…» (Letter of the Mayor of Piacenza, Rovera, to Mother Rose).

Evidently these are charitable works, vast and complex, which cannot be carried out by persons impaired from the psychic point of view: the reality successfully faced by the Servant of God required capacity of intelligence, of decision, of organizational talent not common.

Charity toward the suffering neighbor: the sick

Mother Rose had from girlhood a particular inclination to the service of the sick and her Institute, while open to relieving any need, had as its principal commitment the care of the infirm at home and in hospitals.

«Her assistance to her grandmother, especially in the illness of 1850, the time of her death, is one of the proofs of her aptitude for giving care to the sick and with love consoling whoever suffers» (Francesco Gattorno, Memoirs, p. 4).

«I went to the Hospital, where I found all my happiness, because nothing discouraged me and nothing disgusted me; cleaning the wounds was the most welcome thing, because it seemed to me I was doing it to my dear Jesus, and so many times I had to seek to distract myself so as not to remain rapt in Him and to abstain from kissing them, because afterward I noticed that the patient said so, for fear that it might become known, so I had noticed» (Memoirs, 1, p. 72).

«Take comfort you who labor for your Jesus. Ah! you always converse with Jesus, you touch Jesus, because in touching those poor sick with charity, and that so great charity which your dear Mother St. Anne had, (you touch) Jesus who is found in them. Ah! at this thought, my daughter, I assure you I feel myself dying from the desire to come, to be with you, to take part in your charity» (Letter to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, 22-3-1871).

«I would have liked to hear of new assistance to the infirm. Let us hope that the good Jesus will deign to let Himself be assisted by the poor daughters of His great Grandmother St. Anne, Mother of the Immaculate» (Letter to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti 22-5-1871).

«How sweet it is to us when we can offer the needy a relief, when we feel awakened in us an entirely pure affection for those creatures, however repugnant; and if he needed our very blood, we would soon draw it from our veins to satisfy the poor or the sick» (Letter to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, 4-2-1871).

«I recommend to you the care of the infirm, go with love, with reverence as if you were going to Jesus; if sleep comes upon me I shall try to rise and do all I can to wake, I must imagine I am before Jesus and that He counts all that I do for this sick person. See, I went there for 25 years and it seemed to me I was going to Paradise, see, there is no consolation on earth but this; I have not felt it any more since I no longer go there. Yes, do everything in a spirit of faith. I am in this Hospital, this woman full of insects I dress her wounds, I relieve her, ah! what a delight to think of relieving a creature of Jesus, yes, there is no office that brings so much consolation as this; to return home in the morning and say: I have dressed the wound of my Jesus!

You will tell me: But I have not experienced these delights; ah! because it means that you have never done it in a spirit of faith, because we let so many labors go in vain; why do we act as if we were so many servants? Ah! yes, the Lord has always looked with an eye of predilection on nurses!» (Notes of a conference given at Ferrara on 4 July, probably of 1874).

I realize I have not been brief; but the importance of the theme required a treatment of the proof material, in order to reach credible conclusions.

The conduct of the Servant of God toward all the persons she met during her earthly existence has been examined: neighbor in general, family, husband, children, relatives, Sisters, superiors, abandoned children, the sick, etc.

We are faced with a vastest variety of persons and circumstances which constitutes a severe and probative test of the psychic balance of a person.

To have dealt with so many persons, to have faced the most diverse and most demanding problems, to have given life to a new, well-organized Institute, of most robust vitality and rapidly grown and spread, until reaching 4,000 sisters in the lifetime of the Foundress, means that she possessed truly superior qualities: not only can one not hypothesize a psychic impairment of the Servant of God, but the facts of her life show convincingly that Mother Gattorno was particularly endowed with rich natural gifts, which she knew how to use in the noblest and worthiest manner, with the exercise of the virtues, constant over time and of high level.

This is a deduction that follows, better, that imposes itself, with the force deriving from concrete facts, amply ascertained.

In effect the whole vast range of the attitude the Servant of God had, during her earthly life, toward the neighbor has been examined.

The awareness deriving from her strong faith, the charge of intense love that made her direct toward God all her thinking, willing, acting, gave a quite precise aspect, with an absolutely supernatural direction, to her relations with the neighbor, whether in the family, or in society in general, or within the Institute, or toward Superiors and toward all those she had to approach as Foundress.

Observing with serenity this broad picture that encloses the life of Anna Rosa Gattorno, we see emerge a woman rich in intelligence, of great organizational capacities, of a personality of superior level; the deeds accomplished over a span of fully 69 years always and in every circumstance show a perfect self-mastery, a clear vision of problems, an unusual intuitive capacity in dealing with the most diverse persons, gifts of will that enabled her to realize her projects in the best way.

All this seems to me more than sufficient to affirm that there are no doubts about the perfect normality and psychic integrity of the Servant of God.

V

MEDICAL AND OTHER QUALIFIED PERSONS' DECLARATIONS

ON THE PHYSICAL-PSYCHIC STATE OF THE SERVANT OF GOD

a) Dr. Giuseppe Montechiari had the Servant of God in his care during the last 12 years of her life: in a first written declaration of 8 May 1900, that is, immediately after the death of the Foundress, the physician specifies that she

«had been affected by interstitial nephritis for about 12 years and for about a year had been subject to attacks of cardiac arrhythmia due to arteriosclerosis».

Three months before her death she was struck by a severe influenza: the condition of the heart worsened so as to foreshadow the catastrophe. Three days before death an enteroperitonitis set in: death is to be attributed exclusively to the old and recent lesions (autograph declaration of Dr. Giuseppe Montechiari).

b) The physician makes not the slightest mention of the psychic condition of the Servant of God, a clear sign that he must have found it normal: this conclusion is explicitly expressed in a second document of Dr. Montechiari: it is indeed a «sworn expert opinion» before the Royal Magistrate of the second District of Rome, on 11 January 1911. This expert opinion concerned the health condition of the Servant of God and was made at the request of Marchioness Anna Carrega: here is its essential content:

The Expert had Anna Rosa Gattorno in his care during the last 12 years of life;

in November 1899 there were no episodes of notable indisposition;

in February 1900 a severe influenza set in;

on 3 May an attack of entero-peritonitis appeared, as a result of which she died on 6 May 1900;

during the acute phase of the illness Prof. Marchiafava was called, who confirmed diagnosis and therapy;

the attending physician went daily to visit the patient and on these occasions met her family, especially her daughter Countess Barbiellini.

The Expert concludes:

«as an expert appraisal I must observe that I had occasion to note in the aforesaid Mrs. Gattorno, Widow Custo, firmness of character and absence of indecision, finding therefore in her no suggestible temperament».

A declaration of this kind, sworn moreover and drawn up at an unsuspicious time, is sufficient to answer, with well-founded motivation, the question put to me.

In the acts, however, there exist other documents concerning the volitional-intellective state of the Servant of God which allow a broader inquiry and therefore more objective conclusions.

c) Declaration of the Notary Mr. Tommaso Monti, who drew up the holograph will of the Servant of God: among other things one reads:

«In the conversations I had with her in this regard, I could note that she, although extremely busy with the dispatch of not a few affairs of her administration, was in good health and of serene and tranquil mind».

d) Declaration of the ordinary Confessor of the Institute, Fr. Vincenzo da Alatri, O.F.M. Cap.: the Father approached the Servant of God during the last three years of life: 22 days after the death of the Foundress he wrote, among other things:

«In a triennium in which I had the honor and good fortune of approaching her, she always gave me proofs of a rectitude, honesty and perfection not common. Endowed by God with the holiest and noblest charisms, she spent her days benefiting all and relieving from so many miseries poor languishing humanity».

The religious then describes at length the last days of the Servant of God, praises her fortitude in suffering, makes known in detail her most pious death and concludes:

«All this for the truth and for the justice of my ministry, as well as for the honor and respect due to the holy soul of the Foundress of the Daughters of St. Anne».

e) There exist then eight other declarations made by persons who knew the Servant of God very closely: these are highly qualified persons, such as Mons. Domenico Serafini (who later became Cardinal of the H.R.C.), Mons. Verga, Mons. Piacenza etc.: all eight declarations confirm in unmistakable words the high spirituality of the Servant of God, her balance, her organizational capacities, her charity: since, however, the originals of these documents do not exist, I did not wish to use them, out of duty of objectivity.

The declaration of Dr. Montechiari, however, his sworn expert opinion, the declaration of the Notary who drew up the will of the Servant of God and the declaration of her Confessor constitute documents of fundamental importance for drawing serious, well-founded conclusions. The authors of these documents are credible, unsuspected persons and direct witnesses of what they assert.

One can therefore be at ease about the objectivity of their statements.

There exist then two other concrete elements of judgment: first of all the life, the virtues of the Servant of God, her way of facing adversities, the great accomplishments, the most pious death: secondly, the comparative examination between the volume «Labors and Consolations…» and the other writings of the Servant of God: «The Memoirs», written on the advice of His Most Eminent Granito di Belmonte, and the 8,487 letters.

VI

CONCLUSION

The material used to elaborate this Vote is very vast, and the individual problems faced, in order to reach objectively founded conclusions, are several; in order therefore to give a logical order to this writing and to make it clearer, I have divided it into six topics:

I - Life of the Servant of God;

II - The volume «Labors and Consolations»;

III - Comparative examination between this work and the other writings of the

Servant of God;

IV - Internal criteria emerging from the writings, for ascertaining the nor-

mal psychic state, or not, of the author;

V - Declarations of the physicians who treated the Servant of

God and of qualified witnesses on the psychophysical state of the

same;

VI - Conclusion.

The study has proved fruitful: it has been possible to ascertain, on the basis of serious and credible documentation, that the whole question which led to the «reponatur» arose from a glaring misunderstanding: it was thought that the volume «Labors and Consolations, etc.» was the history of a soul, whereas instead it is the history of an Institute, which is very different. The Servant of God, in fact, did not want to write the history of the Institute for two reasons:

a) she did not want to put herself in evidence and

b) she found it repugnant to make known the difficulties encountered, so as not to reveal the names of the authors.

It was Cardinal Granito Pignatelli di Belmonte, Princess Emilia di Fitalia and some Sisters who insistently asked Gattorno to write the history of the Institute.

The Servant of God, for the two reasons stated, wished

«artfully to hide this history under figures, allegories and other things, so that the mission she had had in this fact of the foundation would not come to be known. I was able to ascertain with certainty what I have said because I was perfectly aware of the facts reported in that book in allegorical form» (Cardinal Granito di Belmonte, Roman Process, Sess. V, fols. 54-56, vol. I).

The solution of the problem is all here: Rosa Gattorno, in the book under discussion, does not speak of herself, but of the Institute: the misunderstanding arose from the fact that the manuscript bore no title and Cardinal Guarino, Archbishop of Messina, on his own initiative, gave it that of «Labors and Consolations of the soul on the way of perfection», a title absolutely improper, as Cardinal Granito di Belmonte lamented in his time (Roman Process, Sess. V, fol. 55, vol. I).

The volume, however, contains nothing against faith and morals, on the contrary: indeed it was repeatedly approved and praised by high ecclesiastical authorities.

The misunderstanding having been cleared, the motivation falls that led the Holy Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith to undertake a study on the state of normality, or not, of the Servant of God.

This first conclusion is well reinforced by the comparative examination of the volume and of all the other writings of Gattorno.

The psychic normality, or not, of a subject can be ascertained by observing two important moments of her life: her conduct toward God and in relations with the various persons.

In this regard I wished to examine the concrete exercise of the virtues of faith and charity, in their twofold aspect toward the Creator and toward the brethren, on the part of the Servant of God; these precious elements of evaluation made it possible to ascertain that faith in God and love for Him were the essential motive of Gattorno's thought and action.

The conduct then of the Foundress in the matter of charity toward the neighbor has made it possible to observe, in all its aspects, the entire complex of her life of relationship: and this is a basic and precious element for a judgment, because the way a subject acts in the face of the various circumstances of life, joyful and sad, painful and exalting, easy and difficult, lays bare her psychological state. In fact, besides the episodes and facts that make up the fabric of daily life, one must bear in mind the great variety of persons involved with the Servant of God in the unfolding of the facts themselves.

In all this complex of facts and persons Gattorno's conduct always appears composed, straightforward, marked by a Christian orientation of life, always followed with persevering consistency, with a markedly supernatural vision.

If we then dwell attention on the content of the facts, we note that these, by their value and by the way in which they were lived, exalt the personality of the Foundress; they not only exclude the possibility of qualifying her as not normal from the psychic point of view, but demonstrate with undeniable force that we are before a subject particularly endowed from the point of view of intelligence, will and psychic balance.

The very book «Labors and Consolations», objectively read in the context in which it was written, constitutes an evident proof of the goodness, prudence and humility of the Servant of God.

It is not my task to report the conclusions that impose themselves in the matter of the exercise of the individual virtues, after reading the writings of the Servant of God: I must, however, make known that the judgment is very positive.

From the medical point of view in general and, particularly, from the point of view of the question to which I must reply, I must admit that the objective ascertainment of the exercise of all the virtues, at a high level and prolonged in time, constitutes a further solid argument to demonstrate that Anna Rosa Gattorno always enjoyed a great psychic balance.

In this place ample and due importance must be given to what was set forth, at a time and in circumstances not suspect, by the physicians who treated the Servant of God, particularly in the last years of her earthly life, and to what highly qualified persons reported on her psychic state; the study made it possible to ascertain that:

1) The physician who had the Servant of God in his care during the last 12 years of life affirms, and decisively, the perfect psychic balance of the patient;

2) The Notary Tommaso Monti, who drew up Gattorno's holograph will, personally ascertained, in repeated conversations, her normality;

3) The Confessor, Fr. Vincenzo da Alatri, uses particularly elevated words in describing the rectitude and uncommon perfection of the Servant of God;

4) Her whole complex existence, the way she lived married life, the circumstances of the foundation and the surprising development of the Institute of the Daughters of St. Anne, demonstrate

p. 893

i

with the proof of facts that Gattorno was not only normal from the psychic point of view, but was a person rich in high qualities;

5) The comparative examination between the work «Labors and Consolations…» and all the other writings of Gattorno shows a perfect self-mastery, a more than notable psychic balance, great accomplishing capacities and (especially in the vast correspondence) a continual exercise of charity in understanding, directing, comforting others.

Consequently, to the doubt proposed about the normality of the Servant of God, I answer that Anna Rosa Gattorno was a person certainly normal from the psychic point of view.

Ready to offer any further clarification that may be asked of me, I extend to You the sentiments of my religious greeting and remain, with all deference,
